newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mostly up, then slips after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mostly up, then slips after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX natgas futures, helped by forecasts for more Arctic weather later this week, ended mostly higher Wednesday in moderate trade, then eased slightly on ACCESS after the weekly AGA inventory report, sources said.
February rallied 21.8 cents to close at $3.611 per million British thermal units, then eased to $3.58 on ACCESS. March settled 14.9 cents higher at $3.145. Most others also ended up.

"Right now, you can't sell it because we have the coldest weather of the season headed east, but later next week, the Midwest and Northeast are supposed to be above-normal," said one East Coast trader.

AGA said late Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 127 bcf, only slightly above expectations and well-below last year's weekly decline of 197 bcf. Total stocks are now 139 bcf, or 7.8 percent above year-ago, with an eastern surplus of 263 bcf, or 27.6 percent, over last year.

"The AGA number was right in the middle of my range. I don't think you can call it bullish or bearish," said another eastern trader, adding light profit taking after a two-day rally was pressuring prices on ACCESS.

With an Arctic freeze expected to blanket the nation into early next week and storage and pipeline withdrawal limits from the cold likely to continue near-term, few expected prices to collapse near-term.
But most agreed the return of more moderate weather could send the market into a tailspin.
Technically, traders now pegged February resistance in the $3.80-3.84 area and then at $3.96. Support was seen in the gap between $3.11 and $3.185 and then in the $2.60s.
Cash prices at the Gulf Coast jumped Wednesday by about 30 cents to the $4.20s and $4.30s. Midcon pipes were assessed in the $5.05-5.10 range, up 80 cents on the day.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 7.3 cents to $2.529. NYMEX said an estimated 47,636 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 38,083.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On the KCBT, February closed 17 cents higher at $3.40, while deferred months finished up by five to 15 cents. The East/West spread widened by 4.8 cents to 21.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 293 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's total of 214.
